Palladium.  Pd.

A  metal  accompanying  Platina  and  Aurum.

Proposed  as  a  remedy  as  early  as  1833.     See  Stapf 's  Archives.

"This  metal  belongs  with  Mercury,  Silver,  Gold,  Platina,  and  others  occurring
in  small  quantities,  like  Iridium,  Rhodium,  Ruthenium,  and  the  very  remarkable

selves, more  easily  separable  from  oxygen  than  the  others,  but  having  greater
affinity  for  Sulphur.  If  we  classify  the  Sulphides  according  to  their  solubility  in
dilute  acids,  Palladium  must  be  placed  with  Argentum,  Rhodium,  Ruthenium  and
Osmium,  and  Platina  remains  with  the  less  soluble  Mercury,  Aurum  and  Iridium.
The  nature  of  solubility  in  dilute  acids  one  would  expect  would  show  itself  in  the
provings.  Platina  and  Palladium  both  proved  in  dust  form  showed  such  sim-
ilarity in  their  effects  that  the  question  arose  whether  corresponding  differences
miglit  be  found.  These  data  can  only  be  furnished  by  frequent  use  of  Palladium
in  practice." — C.  Hg.,  N.  A.  J.  H.,  vol.  9,  new  series,  p.  129.
